theory.intro: A quadrilateral is **convex** when all four interior angles are less than $180^{\circ}$. If one interior angle is reflex — bigger than $180^{\circ}$ — it is **non-convex** (or concave) and its outline has a dent.
facts: **Convex**: every interior angle is less than $180^{\circ}$.
Diagonal test: in a convex quadrilateral both diagonals lie inside the shape and meet inside it.
A square, a rectangle, a rhombus and a parallelogram are all convex.
steps: Look around the outline for a vertex that points back into the shape — a dent.
Check the interior angle at that vertex: is it more than $180^{\circ}$?
One reflex interior angle makes it non-convex; if every interior angle is less than $180^{\circ}$ it is convex.

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) All four vertices point outwards. Every interior angle is less than $180^{\circ}$, so it is convex.
(b) The outline turns inwards at $C$. The interior angle at $C$ is reflex, so it is non-convex.

workedExamples.question_text:
Decide whether each quadrilateral is convex or non-convex. Give a reason.
(a) Its interior angles are $135^{\circ}$, $85^{\circ}$, $75^{\circ}$ and $65^{\circ}$.
(b) Its interior angles are $225^{\circ}$, $55^{\circ}$, $45^{\circ}$ and $35^{\circ}$.
(c) It is a rectangle.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Every angle is less than $180^{\circ}$, so it is convex.
(b) $225^{\circ}$ is reflex. One reflex interior angle makes it non-convex.
(c) All four angles of a rectangle are $90^{\circ}$. None is reflex, so it is convex.

(a) Both diagonals lie inside the outline and cross inside it. The quadrilateral is convex.
(b) Diagonal $BD$ lies outside the outline. The quadrilateral is non-convex.
(c) One diagonal inside is not enough. Both must lie inside for a convex quadrilateral. $BD$ lies outside, and the interior angle at $C$ is reflex.

practice.coverageNote: Foundation, Development and Mastery use the booklet's figure-classification task, with less obvious dents and thinner or rotated figures in the harder tiers.

foundation.solution_text:
Every vertex points outwards, so no interior angle is reflex.
Convex

The angle at the lowest vertex is close to a straight angle, but it is still less than $180^{\circ}$, and so is every other angle.
Convex

The outline turns inwards at the middle vertex, giving a reflex interior angle there.
Non-convex

Every vertex points outwards, so every interior angle is less than $180^{\circ}$.
Convex

The outline turns inwards at the vertex between the top and leftmost vertices. Its interior angle is reflex.
Non-convex

The outline turns back on itself at $D$, where the interior angle is greater than $180^{\circ}$.
Non-convex

All four vertices point outwards. None of the interior angles is reflex.
Convex

development.solution_text:
Each dashed diagonal stays inside the outline, and the two diagonals cross inside the shape.
Convex, because the diagonals meet inside the quadrilateral.

One diagonal lies outside the outline, so the two diagonal segments do not cross inside the shape.
Non-convex, because one of the diagonals lies outside the quadrilateral.

The shape is long and thin, but the outline still turns back on itself at the middle vertex.
The interior angle there is bigger than $180^{\circ}$.
Non-convex

The vertex between the rightmost and top vertices makes a shallow dent. Its interior angle is greater than $180^{\circ}$.
Non-convex

At $G$ the outline turns back into the shape, so its interior angle is greater than $180^{\circ}$.
Non-convex

Although the shape is thin and one angle is close to a straight angle, every vertex points outwards. All interior angles are less than $180^{\circ}$.
Convex

mastery.solution_text:
The vertex between the rightmost and top vertices makes a shallow inward turn. Its interior angle is greater than $180^{\circ}$.
Non-convex

The thin, rotated outline has no dent. Even the nearly straight interior angle is less than $180^{\circ}$.
Convex
